title: The check-timeout refusal names `verdict <cmd>`, a bare command that is not on PATH in a cloud session; it names the full path
why: Coordinator 01:27 CST Nov 14 (lane combine-g1, relayed; unchecked by triage): the check-timeout remedy says "start it in the background, as `verdict <cmd>`", and the lane's `command -v verdict` printed nothing in its cloud box. CORRECTED 01:37 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 01:28, g1's own read, relayed; the first relay said "not installed", unchecked): the file exists at /root/.claude/bin/verdict in that box (dated 07:25 UTC); it is off PATH, so the printed remedy `verdict <cmd>` fails for want of PATH. Not yet tried: whether the background form `~/.claude/bin/verdict python3 merge/merge.py <pr> --lane-lint` passes the worktree guard (unknown). In triage's own session the tool exists at ~/.claude/bin/verdict, and a builder earlier ran it as `/root/.claude/bin/verdict python3 lint/test_rule_audit.py` (lane shared-savings-gap-read), so the cause is that the folder is not on PATH, not that verdict is missing (confirmed by g1, relayed).
source: Coordinator 01:27 CST Nov 14 (relayed). Neighbours: lane-lint-in-isolated-worktree (ready: the second refusal the lane hit), lane-lint-bg-timeout (doing), lane-lint-cloud-time-limit (doing). A remedy never names the forbidden target (rule git-remedy-never-names-target).
note: Triage 01:35 CST Nov 14: the harm: an agent that follows the refusal's remedy to the letter runs a command the shell cannot find, and then stops or asks for an override it did not need. Fix: the lane first runs `command -v verdict` and `ls ~/.claude/bin/verdict` in a cloud lane session and says whether it is missing or only off PATH. Then, red first: the check-timeout refusal text names the form that runs in that box (the full path, or the install step), and a test pins the text against the constant the guard emits (rule building-allow-list-is-the-constant). A guard text change: own lane, or folded into the lane that takes lane-lint-bg-timeout. Not started.
